page: Microsoft Azure E16-4ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provisions 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical execution cores with multithreading enabled. It includes 128 GB of system memory, providing a high density of 32 GB of RAM per vCPU, alongside a bundled 644 GB local SSD for high-speed scratch storage. No GPU coprocessors are provisioned on this instance type.

The underlying x86_64 architecture supports instruction extensions including AVX-512, VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI. Synthetic benchmarks reflect solid single-thread performance alongside restricted multi-core aggregate throughput due to the low physical core count. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1629.0 and a multi-core score of 3499.0, complemented by a stress-ng single-core score of 1896.98. Potentially uncached large-block memory bandwidth tests measure 28.87 GB/sec for reads and 25.23 GB/sec for writes.

By constraining vCPU count while retaining a 128 GB memory pool, this configuration provides architectural cost efficiency for software with licensing structures tied directly to core counts. The primary tradeoff is bounded parallel processing capability, as evidenced by Redis SET operations achieving 3.98 million operations per second and modest compression throughput. The instance is suited for in-memory caching tiers, memory-intensive ETL pipelines, and relational database management systems that require substantial buffer pools without extensive CPU parallelism.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-4ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, accompanied by 128 GB of system memory and 644 GB of local SSD storage without GPU acceleration. The extreme 32 GB per vCPU memory allocation targets workloads with high memory footprints but modest parallel compute requirements. Performance metrics show average single-thread results, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1629.0, whereas multi-core throughput is constrained by the 4-vCPU limit at a score of 3499.0. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 28.87 GB/sec. Because licensing or resource allocation can be pinned to lower vCPU counts while retaining high RAM, the instance provides cost efficiency for memory-bound tasks. It is suited for in-memory caches, small-to-midsize relational databases, and data processing jobs.
